name: binance-files
notes: Gates over the inventory of any Binance Vision httpblobs pull (klines or BVOL): one row per requested day with status ok or refused. The files themselves are hashed into the snapshot manifest and re-checked by `verify`; this suite checks the inventory. A refused day (Binance lacks it, or it would not reshape) is a WARN: the pull tolerates max_refused of them so a gap is visible and decided, not fatal. Run: python -m dskit.onboarding validate --suite configs/suite-binance-files.json --snapshot <snapshot-vid> --root <store root>.

rules.notes: One row per requested day, ok or refused; none means nothing was requested.
Each refused day is a hole in the series. Read `reason` and `http_status` in the inventory before modelling across it.
A stored parquet of zero bytes is a writer defect (refused rows carry no size).
